I spent the last hour searching Quora and LinkedIn to see if people respect this company, just to prove to myself that I didn't fail again. I hate that his one sentence wiped out all my hard work.

We are building our final year project and every time I write a module, I ask my team lead like five times if it's okay or if I should rewrite the whole thing. Every time I open LinkedIn and see someone posting about getting a 6-month internship or winning some hackathon, I feel this sick urge to post something too, even though I have nothing to show. I actually spent half an hour drafting a post about completing a basic 2-hour Coursera course just to get some likes and feel like I'm still in the race. I deleted the draft because I felt so pathetic. Why do I need random internet strangers to validate that my life isn't a total waste of space?

I finally cracked a 3-star rating on CodeChef today after coding for 6 hours straight in the lab, but honestly, it felt like nothing. The moment I saw my roommate post his FAANG internship offer in our class WhatsApp group, I immediately deleted my LinkedIn draft. Why can't I just feel happy about my own progress without needing fifty people to like my post or my prof to tell me I did good?

I spent my entire weekend rewriting my DSA lab report because my partner said my logic was 'a bit long'. I haven't submitted it yet because I'm literally shaking waiting for my TA to reply to my email asking if my approach is okay. I feel like a toddler who can't take a single step without holding someone's hand, like my own brain is completely untrustworthy.

My dad called me today to ask if I got my midterm grades back for DBMS, and before I could even tell him I scored a 42/50, he started talking about how Sharma ji's son got a 12 LPA package. I just shut up and didn't mention my marks because what's the point if it's never the 'right' success? I’m 21 and I’m still begging for a 'good job, beta' that I know is never coming.

We were dividing tasks for our capstone project today, and when I suggested using MongoDB, everyone just ignored me until the topper suggested the exact same thing five minutes later and everyone cheered. I spent the rest of the class silent, frantically googling if my database concept was actually stupid or if I'm just invisible. I feel like unless a 'smart' person validates my words, they don't exist.

My whole self-worth is literally hanging on a PDF offer letter.
